\(\angle ABC = \angle AED = 90^\circ\) (given)

\(\angle BAC = \angle EAD\) (common angle A)

Therefore \(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta AED\) (AA similarity).

**(b)** In right \(\Delta ABC\), by Pythagoras' theorem:

\(BC = \sqrt{AC^2 - AB^2} = \sqrt{25^2 - 20^2} = \sqrt{625 - 400} = \sqrt{225} = 15\) cm.

Since \(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta AED\), the corresponding sides are proportional:

\(\frac{AB}{AE} = \frac{BC}{ED} = \frac{AC}{AD}\)

\(\frac{BC}{ED} = \frac{15}{3} = 5\).

So \(AE = \frac{AB}{5} = \frac{20}{5} = 4\) cm and \(AD = \frac{AC}{5} = \frac{25}{5} = 5\) cm.

**(c)** Area of \(\Delta ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times BC = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 15 = 150\) cm\(^2\).

Area of \(\Delta AED = \frac{1}{2} \times AE \times DE = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3 = 6\) cm\(^2\).

Area of BCED on the map \(= 150 - 6 = 144\) cm\(^2\).

Actual area \(= 576\) m\(^2 = 576 \times 10000\) cm\(^2\).

If the scale factor is \(k\), then \(k^2 = \frac{\text{map area}}{\text{actual area}} = \frac{144}{5760000}\), so \(k = \frac{12}{2400} = \frac{1}{200}\).

The scale factor of the map is \(1 : 200\) (1 cm on the map represents 2 m on the ground).

\(\angle PTR = \angle TSR = \angle PST\) (the angle between the tangent PT and the chord TR equals the angle in the alternate segment)

Therefore \(\Delta PTR \sim \Delta PST\) (AA similarity).

**(b)** Since \(\Delta PTR \sim \Delta PST\), corresponding sides are proportional:

\(\frac{PT}{PS} = \frac{PR}{PT}\)

So \(PT^2 = PR \times PS\). Hence proved.

**(c)** \(PT^2 = 4 \times 16 = 64\), so \(PT = 8\) cm.

The ogive passes through (2000, 10), (4000, 20), (6000, 35), (8000, 55), (10000, 70) and (12000, 75). So the classes are 0-2000, 2000-4000, ..., 10000-12000, and the cumulative frequency at each upper limit is read off the graph.

**(a)** The last point is (12000, 75), so the total number of workers \(N = 75\).

**(b)** Median is the \(\frac{N}{2} = \frac{75}{2} = 37.5^{th}\) value. The cumulative frequency is 35 at ₹6000 and 55 at ₹8000, so 37.5 falls in the class **₹6000 - ₹8000**. This is the median class.

**(c)** Lower quartile is the \(\frac{N}{4} = \frac{75}{4} = 18.75^{th}\) value. The cumulative frequency is 10 at ₹2000 and 20 at ₹4000, so 18.75 falls in the class **₹2000 - ₹4000**. This is the lower-quartile class.

**(d)** Workers with salary less than ₹10000 = 70; workers with salary less than ₹6000 = 35.

Number with salary \(\ge\) ₹6000 but \(<\) ₹10000 \(= 70 - 35 = 35\).
